summary: Panic Buyer round 3: capped ladder, take-profit vs 24h high, time-of-day, and a noise band; adversarially verify any pass

result.task: ladder: round 2's split ladder (r2_crowding.py H2) with the coin's total (both legs) capped at 20% or 25% of equity. One pre-registered grid of 8 variants, run once through study.study(). Note: this family was already looked at on 2024-26 in round 2, and this grid was written after those results were known, so 2024-26 is not a clean test here; only the reserved 2018-20 holdout could decide it.

hypotheses.name: Capped split ladder: w of the coin's budget at the 12% trigger, 1-w resting at ref*(1-d2); both legs together capped at 1/N of equity (25% on 4 coins, 20% on 5)
hypotheses.rationale: Round 2's split ladder (50% at 12% / 50% at 18%, 4 coins) beat live in 2021-23 and 2024-26 but failed the LUNA/FTT/SRM check. Its per-coin cap of 20%/w let one coin hold up to 40% of equity (one LUNA trade in May 2021 at 40.0% of equity lost 47.4%). Here fmax caps the coin's TOTAL budget a = min(fmax x equity, cash/nsel), and a is split w / 1-w between the two legs. Both legs rest from the hour start and are fully funded; leg-2 cash is locked until it fills or the position is sold, and an unfilled leg 2 is cancelled when the position sells. After leg 2 fills, the take-profit is the average cost x 1.015, placed at the next hourly cycle. The 48h time stop and 24h cooldown count from the first leg's fill. The cap is tied to N (1/N), so at full cash the N coins can use all the money, like live's 8 x 12.5%. Grid, fixed before any capped variant was run: w {1/2, 2/3} x (N, cap) {(4, 25%), (5, 20%)} x d2 {18%, 20%} = 8. d2 = 16% was left out because round 2's 2021-23 numbers gave it the deepest drops in both families (-41%, -34%). New kernel: lkernel in r3_ladder.py, a copy of the current engine.gkernel (including mtp_now) with the ladder added. With w=1 it is bit-identical to engine.run in all 6 combinations: 19 coins / +dead x normal / 0.2% worse fills, plus mtp_now=True for 19 coins and +dead. With the ladder on and mtp_now off it is bit-identical to round 2's r2_crowding.crun on 96 ladder runs (r3_ladder_xcheck.py). All 7 hand-made one-coin paths pass, including the cap binding, locked leg-2 cash in equity, and mtp_now market buys. engine.run was pointed at lrun in memory only.

result.key_findings:
1. Capping the coin's total does not rescue the split ladder. The pick on 2021-23 was the round 2 design with a 25% cap: 50% at 12% / 50% at 18%, 4 coins. It passed steps 1-3: 2021-23 x8.85 / -22.6% / 2022 +39%; 2024-26 x2.67 / -15.1%; fills 0.2% worse x7.41 / x2.49. It failed step 4: with LUNA/FTT/SRM, 2021-23 is x5.16 with a -44.2% drop, against live's x5.22 / -31.4%. Live bot unchanged; no holdout candidate.
2. The 2024-26 'pass' is not new evidence. For the pick, the cap never binds in 2024-26: no budget went above 25% there, uncapped or capped. Its 2024-26 equity curve is the same as round 2's uncapped pick (x2.6723 both). The 5-coin variant's 2024-26 result (x2.7272) is likewise the same as its round-2 uncapped version. The family had already been seen on 2024-26, so this is restated as contaminated; only 2018-20 could judge it, and with step 4 failed it does not go there.
3. Why it fails: concentration across coins, not in one coin. With 4 coins at up to 25% each and averaging down, a correlated cascade puts almost all equity into the fastest-falling, high-beta coins. In May 2021 that was LUNA, SOL, SRM and NEAR, each with both legs filled, losing 30-47%. The cap cut the single LUNA hit from -19.0% to -11.9% of equity. The total in that window was still -40.1% (live -20.2%), so the drop only went from -49.0% to -44.2%. On the 19 live coins alone the same ladder is excellent in 2021-23 (-22.6% drop vs live's -29.2%). The extra losses come from the collapse coins, which the 'closest 4 coins' rule selects first.
4. Post-hoc, informational only: none of the 8 capped variants beats live in both periods with LUNA/FTT/SRM, so no setting in this grid would have passed all four steps. If this idea is pursued again, the lever is total exposure to second legs across coins (e.g. how many coins may average down at once), not the per-coin cap. That would be a new post-hoc idea on a family whose 2024-26 data is used up; it would need the holdout or forward data.
5. Code: lkernel (r3_ladder.py) is bit-identical to engine.run with the ladder off, including mtp_now=True, and to round 2's crun with it on (96 runs). lrun has engine.run's signature plus d2 and w, and works on any panel. result.task: tphigh: take-profit set part of the way back to the reference 24h high, sell at entry + f x (ref_at_entry - entry), with or without a +1.5% floor, instead of a fixed +1.5%

hypotheses.name: H1 take-profit at entry + f x (ref - entry): (A) no floor, f in {0.08, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25}; (B) max(+1.5%, f x gap), f in {0.06, 0.08, 0.10}
hypotheses.rationale: The take-profit is set relative to the trigger's own reference (the highest close of the 24 closed hourly candles before the entry hour) and the actual fill price. It is placed at the next hourly cycle as in the live bot, and everything else is unchanged. For a limit fill, entry = 0.88 x ref, so the gap is 13.64% of entry and the rule is just a fixed take-profit of f x 13.64% (f=0.11 is +1.5%, f=0.125 is +1.70%). The two rules differ only on market buys, where the open was already under the trigger, which are deeper and in 2021-23 bounced back in proportion to the drop. Family A is the pure rule, with limit-fill targets from 1.09% to 3.41%. Family B keeps the live +1.5% on limit fills and asks more from deep market buys. A floor only changes anything when f < 0.11, so a floored f >= 0.11 would have duplicated family A. That is why the suggested grid {0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25} x {floor, no floor} was turned into 5 unfloored + 3 floored variants. Engine: tkernel is gkernel copied with one per-entry input tpf[t,k]: tpp = max(fill*(1+tp[t,k]), fill + tpf[t,k]*(ref[t,k]-fill)). tp is the floor and tp=-1 means no floor. The target uses the actual fill price, so under fills 0.2% worse it is computed from the worse fill. This choice was declared in the docstring before the run.

result.key_findings:
Rejected. The live bot stays unchanged. The 8-variant grid was fixed in /home/user/halal-rider/research/panic_buyer/refine/r3_tphigh.py before anything ran and was run once through study.study(), with engine.run pointed at trun in memory only. The 2021-23 pick 'tp = 0.10 x (ref - entry), no floor' beat live in 2021-23 (x6.65 / -29% / 2022 +32% vs x5.75 / -29% / +19%), in 2024-26 (x2.63 / -16% vs x2.61 / -16%) and with LUNA/FTT/SRM (x6.43 | x2.63 vs x5.22 | x2.61). It failed fills 0.2% worse in 2024-26 (x2.23 vs x2.37).

What the tests show:
(1) For about 90% of entries the 'ref-relative' take-profit is just a fixed take-profit. Limit fills sit exactly 13.64% below ref, so f only re-levels the target (f=0.10 gives 1.36%, f=0.25 gives 3.41%). The rule differs from live only on market buys: 175 of 1,681 trades in 2021-23 and 58 of 884 in 2024-26.
(2) The real effect is on those deep market buys, and it is a 2021-22 effect. They bounced back in proportion to the drop, and taking f x gap raised their contribution from +0.33 to +0.92 start-of-period equity (pick) or +0.80 (floored f=0.10). In 2024-26 there are too few deep market buys for it to matter (+0.02 live vs +0.05 pick).
(3) The unfloored pick also cuts the limit-fill target from 1.5% to 1.36%. With normal fills that is a wash in 2024-26 (a tie inside the live jitter band x2.58..x2.77). With fills 0.2% worse, the smaller per-trade margin costs it (limit-fill net +1.20 vs +1.34), and it fails.
(4) Larger f (0.15-0.25) means longer holds and deeper drops: -35% to -39% in 2021-23 and -19% to -24% in 2024-26. This is the same 'earns more only by dropping deeper' pattern rounds 1-2 found.
(5) Engine: tkernel/trun reproduce engine.run exactly with the new switch off (4 configurations, np.array_equal), and match engine.run fed a per-entry tp array to <= 1.7e-14. Spec features ({'tp': -1.0 or 0.015, 'tpf': f}) are plain scalars, so they would work on any panel; no holdout candidate is offered.

result.task: timeofday: do dips bought in thin hours (Asian-morning UTC hours, weekends) behave differently? Analysis of 2021-23 live trades by UTC hour and weekday of the order placement, then 2 hypotheses x 8 variants run once through study.study() on the stock engine.run

hypotheses.name: H1 Asian-morning hours (UTC 00-07 or 03-06, every day): skip, deeper trigger or half size
hypotheses.rationale: In 2021-23 the weak live entries were the ones placed in the Asian morning, not in thin hours in general. Inside the window only: skip = smult 0, so no order goes out in those hours; a coin still under its 12% trigger when the window ends is bought at market at that hour's open. depth 14% / 16% = trigger at the 24h high x (1-d). half = smult 0.5. Everything else is the live bot. The hour is the UTC open time of the hourly cycle in which the order is placed, P['o'].index, so it works on any panel.

result.key_findings:
Verdict: no change to the live bot. Neither hypothesis passes, and no holdout_candidate() was added. The rule ran unchanged: grids fixed in /home/user/halal-rider/research/panic_buyer/refine/r3_timeofday.py before any result, each grid run once, stock engine.run, no bugs found. Logs and CSVs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-halal-rider/ec562e35-ea9e-5a74-ab92-4ff22c5eeb77/scratchpad/pb_out_r3/timeofday/ (motiv.log, motiv2.log, r3_timeofday.log, posthoc.log, r3_timeofday_h1_asia.csv, r3_timeofday_h2_weekend.csv, verdicts.csv).

1) In 2021-23 the weak hours were the Asian session, not thin hours as such. The thinnest hours by volume are UTC 03-05 and 21-23. But 20-23 had some of the best entries (avg +1.49%, 3.9% time stops), while the Asian morning UTC 00-07 was weak in every year: avg +0.39% vs +1.27% outside, time stops 9.7% vs 4.9%. Within that, UTC 03-06 averaged -0.15% and weekend 00-07 -0.64%. Hour 14 UTC was also weak (100 trades, avg -0.81%), but it is a busy hour and was not tested. Over a whole weekend the effect was small and absent in 2022, and whole-weekend filters lost even in 2021-23.

2) The 2021-23 gains were large. Sat-Sun 00-07 skip gave x7.49 with a -24% drop against live x5.75 / -29%. 6 of 16 variants beat live in 2021-23.

3) The effect did not hold in 2024-26. In every year 2024, 2025 and 2026, live trades inside each window did as well as or better than trades outside (r3_timeofday_posthoc.py, post-hoc). For example, Sat-Sun 00-07 entries returned +1.98%, +1.30% and +2.30% with 0 time stops, against +1.21%, +0.82% and +1.16% outside. All 16 variants have a lower 2024-26 multiple than live (best x2.57 vs x2.61), so 0 of 16 beat live in 2024-26.

4) Changing the window also shifts which coins the bot holds when a crash comes. Every skip or deeper-trigger variant, apart from the whole-weekend 16% trigger, has a 2024-26 worst drop of -18% to -21%, against -16% for live. For both picks the worst drop is the 2-3 Feb 2025 crash: -19.6% and -20.6% peak to trough, against -15.4% and -15.5% for live over the same hours. The picks entered it with 10 positions, 117-121% of equity at cost, mostly bought Sunday 16:00-17:00 UTC, outside the window. Live's own worst drop is 2-13 Apr 2024 at -16.3%. Only the half-size and whole-weekend variants kept a -16% or shallower drop, and they earn less (x2.14-2.48).

Time of day or weekday of the order is not a usable filter for this bot: what looked like a consistent 2021-23 effect turned around in 2024-26.
result.near_misses: No variant came within reach in 2024-26: none had a higher 2024-26 multiple than live (x2.61). Closest by multiple: UTC 03-06 depth 14% (the H1 pick) at x2.57, but with a -20% drop against -16%. Closest that kept the drop: Sat-Sun 00-07 half size, 21-23 x6.05 DD -27% | 24-26 x2.48 DD -16%, and UTC 03-06 half size, 21-23 x6.00 DD -29% | 24-26 x2.47 DD -16%. Both beat live in 2021-23 but fall about 0.13 short in 2024-26, a real gap rather than a tie. With fills 0.2% worse and with LUNA/FTT/SRM added, both picks still miss in 2024-26.

result.method:
I measured this without a grid or a pick. Script: /home/user/halal-rider/research/panic_buyer/refine/r3_noise.py (one full run, 388 s). /home/user/halal-rider/research/panic_buyer/refine/r3_noise_summary.py only reads the saved runs. Outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-halal-rider/ec562e35-ea9e-5a74-ab92-4ff22c5eeb77/scratchpad/pb_out_r3/noise/: r3_noise.log, r3_noise_runs.csv, r3_noise_bands.csv, r3_noise_nearmiss.csv, r3_noise_bootstrap.csv, r3_noise_paired.csv and r3_noise_summary.log. The smoke/ folder holds an earlier code-path test with 2 random draws; the fixed perturbations gave the same numbers there.

(1) Live settings, backtest timing, each of the 15 perturbations alone: depth 11.9/12.1%, fee 0.095/0.105%, eps 0.09/0.11%, cap 19/21%, and start +1..7 days. Each period is measured from its own start. For 2021-23 that is a run started at 2021-01-01+d. For 2024-26 it is a fresh run (all cash) started at 2024-01-01+d. The band is min..max of the 15 runs, and sd is their standard deviation (ddof 1). For a steadier sd I also ran 100 random draws with all five perturbations at once (seed 20261022). I measured the same bands with LUNA/FTT/SRM added and with fills 0.2% worse.

(2) Every near miss was re-run under the same perturbations as live (paired), using the spec and runner from its own round 1-2 script. A depth or cap change is applied to the variant's own setting. The tie rule was fixed in the docstring before any result: a gap is a tie when the near miss's value lies inside live's 15-run range. I also report the paired win counts.

(3) Paired circular block bootstrap of the 2024-26 monthly returns, live vs the split ladder: 34 months, blocks of 1, 3 and 6 months, 20,000 resamples each.

Code checks, all passed:
- Starting later by slicing the panel gives exactly the full run with buying blocked before the start.
- trun, crun and lrun with their switches off give exactly engine.run.
- All 9 bots reproduce their reported numbers, e.g. live 5.7500/2.6088, entry H2 6.2622/2.5985, ladder 9.0738/2.6723, 16h 2.6139.

No code bugs found. No existing file was edited and nothing was committed.

result.near_misses_judged:
Near misses against live's 15-run band. "Paired" counts how often the near miss beats live under the same perturbation.

**Entry H2 (r1h>0 & knife, 16% depth)**
- 2024-26 x2.5985 vs x2.6088: gap -0.0102 (-0.14 sd), a TIE. It is never better, though. Its multiple is higher in only 1 of the 15 named runs and 25 of the 100 random draws; the paired gap averages -0.0045 (sd 0.0059). In the bootstrap it has the higher multiple 21.6% of the time (3-month blocks).
- 2021-23 x6.2622 vs x5.7500 (+2.1 sd): a real gain.
- With LUNA/FTT/SRM, the 2021-23 drop -33.33% vs -31.44% is a TIE by the band. But it is more than 1 point deeper in 14 of the 15 named runs and 84 of the 100 draws, so that failure is consistent.
- Fills 0.2% worse, 2024-26 x2.3653 vs x2.3675: a TIE (46/100).
- Verdict: a tie, not a loss and not a gain.

**Trigger 16h window**
- 2024-26 x2.6139 vs x2.6088 (+0.07 sd): a TIE. Paired it is higher in 6/15 and 0/100 (mean gap -0.117); the bootstrap gives 47.9%. Its "beat" is noise.
- 2021-23 x4.5561 (-4.8 sd): a real loss.

**Round-2 split ladder (50% at 12% / 50% at 18%, 4 coins)**
- 2021-23 x9.0738, drop -23.45%: a real gain (+13.4 sd; drop 5.8 points shallower).
- 2024-26 x2.6723 vs x2.6088 (+0.87 sd): a TIE. Its drop -15.12% vs -16.28% is outside the band, but fragile. Depth 12.1% gives x2.633 with a -20.33% drop. In the random draws its multiple is higher only 40/100 and its drop is within 1 point 59/100. It beats live in both periods in 40/100.
- The LUNA/FTT/SRM failure (-48.96% vs -31.44%, -18.9 sd, 0/100 paired) is real.

**Stress-N x=5% N=5**
- 2021-23 x5.9594 (+0.84 sd) and drop -31.45% (2.2 points deeper): both TIEs by the band. But the drop is more than 1 point deeper in 14 of the 15 named runs and 84 of the 100 draws.
- 2024-26 x2.7172 (+1.48 sd): a TIE by the band, yet consistently higher (15/15 and 100/100; paired gap +0.117, sd 0.018; bootstrap 84.4%).
- With LUNA/FTT/SRM its 2021-23 drop -37.77% vs -31.44% (-6.3 points, 0/100) is a real failure.

**Others**
- calm-deeper 2%/+4% (round-1 pick): its 2021-23 "beat" (x5.7655, +0.06 sd) was a tie. 2024-26 x2.1384 is a real loss (-6.4 sd).
- Losers "break-even +0.5% after 24h": x5.7043 and x2.5820 are ties, but it is lower in 0/100 draws... it never comes out higher in 2024-26 (0/100).
- Trigger 12h/11%: 2024-26 x2.5424 (-0.9 sd) and, with fills 0.2% worse, x2.3458 vs x2.3675 are both ties. Its 2021-23 drop of -19.8% is a real gain (+9.4 sd).
- Take-profit after 2 hourly cycles: its 2024-26 drop -20.09% is really deeper (-11 sd).
result.summary:
Live's numbers move a lot under changes that should not matter.
- 2021-23 multiple: x5.17 to x6.09 (sd 0.25); drop -33.1% to -29.1% (sd 1.0 point).
- 2024-26 multiple: x2.52 to x2.77 (sd 0.07); drop -17.1% to -15.6% (sd 0.34 point).

Every round 1-2 near miss in 2024-26 is inside the band, so all are ties: entry H2 -0.010, trigger 16h +0.005, split ladder +0.064, stress-N +0.108. The round-1 calm-deeper pick's 2021-23 edge (+0.016) was also a tie.

Paired re-runs separate a tie that leans one way from one that doesn't:
- Stress-N is consistently higher in 2024-26 (100/100) but consistently more than 1 point deeper in 2021-23, and it fails badly with LUNA/FTT/SRM (-37.8%).
- Entry H2 is consistently a hair lower in 2024-26.
- The ladder's 2024-26 lead holds in only 40/100 combined draws, and one 0.1-point depth change turns its 2024-26 drop into -20.3%.

Bootstrap, live vs split ladder, 2024-26 (34 months: 13 better, 16 worse, mean +0.07 point a month, t 0.22):
- The ladder's multiple is higher in 59.5%, 58.8% and 60.1% of resamples (1, 3 and 6-month blocks).
- It wins under the rule, with the drop measured on month-end values, in 51.4%, 49.6% and 51.9%.
- Its 90% range for ladder/live is 0.85 to 1.23 (3-month blocks).

So the ladder's 2024-26 edge is a coin flip. Its 2021-23 edge is real, and its LUNA/FTT/SRM failure is far beyond noise.

For the holdout and round 3: a 2024-26 multiple gap under about ±0.07 (1 sd) and any 2021-23 drop gap of 1-4 points should be read as ties. The 1-point drop allowance is smaller than the 2021-23 noise.
